what_this_is: The Workshop row for the person's own records in tools/live-records: tool:your-records, the session the engine keeps open and reaches by calls through its one door.

payload.label: Your records
payload.job: Every record the person keeps, read, listed, searched, written and recovered by receipt, and the workspace labels, for the engine's one records door, over the person's own database
payload.description: The person's own records (tools/live-records) as a session the engine keeps open and reaches only by calls: tools:run at @tools {tool: "tool:your-records", call: {name, arguments}} sends one MCP tools/call to the account's one session of this row, which the first call starts (trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools/sessions.rs `call`); each call is answered on its own. `name` is an operation of the records door (tools/records-door/README.md): records:read, records:list, records:search, records:write, records:result, workspace:read and workspace:write. The answer is {tool, result} with the operation's answer in result.structuredContent; a refusal is result.isError with {code, outcome}. An answer too big for one message is a byte page, and the same call with after_byte set to its next_after_byte answers the next. The run opens no port. Its records are rows in the person's own Postgres database (own-rows-postgres-connection, reached on the loopback port the computer reports as own-rows-postgres). The program is the live-records this computer keeps among its program folders.

output_schema.description: A call answers {tool, result: {structuredContent, content, isError}} or {tool, error}; the session's start answers its state.

provenance.source: tools/live-namespace's row store (src/store, now the shared crate tools/live-records/rows-store), over the records door contract of tools/records-door and the former engine record store's door (trillion-workshop tools/keep-lists-of-rows/account-state at 6d6702b8b4, record_value and local_workspace)
